newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli police jailed for beating Arabs.
newsitem.headline: Israeli police jailed for beating Arabs.

text.p: An Israeli court on Thursday sentenced to eight months in jail two paramilitary border policemen filmed brutalising Palestinians and other policemen suspected of similar offences were arrested.
The Jerusalem Magistrates Court ordered Tsahi Shamaya, 19, and David Ben Abu, 20, to serve eight months in prison and gave them a further 12 months suspended sentence.
"The two policemen degraded the border police uniform and must receive a punishment that will deter others," Israel Radio quoted the judge as saying.

The verdict was issued a day after the Israeli rights group B'Tselem released a 31-page report detailing what it said were 15 cases of "beatings, degradation and serious abuse" of Palestinians by security forces over the last three months.
Shamaya and Ben Abu were filmed by an amateur cameraman last October assaulting six Palestinians caught in Jerusalem without entry permits.

The videotape showed the two policemen kicking some of the Palestinians in the head, kneeing one in the stomach, forcing others to do push-ups and riding one man like a donkey. It was broadcast around the world.
The men were charged with aggravated assault and abuse of authority.
Witnesses said relatives of the convicted policemen erupted from their seats in rage after hearing the sentence. One woman was evicted for calling the judge a "leftist".

"I think it will be difficult for a Jewish mother to send her son to the army in light of a verdict like this because the punishment is quite severe," defence lawyer Sasi Gez told reporters. Gez said he would appeal.
B'Tselem activist Yuval Ginbar said officers and not just policemen must be held accountable for police brutality.
"There is something much more rotten here than one or two apples," Ginbar said.
"Beating and ill-treatment of Palestinians, especially at roadblocks and especially by the border police, is a very widespread and very serious phenomenon," he told Reuters.

A Justice Ministry official said several other border policemen were arrested on Thursday in connection with what Israel's Channel One television reported as another case of police brutality involving two Palestinian workers.
The television said in a report on Wednesday the two were so badly beaten that they required hospital treatment.
The television interviewed Palestinian cousins Ahmed Moussa, 19, and Mahmoud Ghneim, 27, who lay side by side in hospital.

It said they were beaten on Tuesday after entering Israel without permits in violation of a closure imposed on the West Bank following a July 30 suicide attack in Israel. Three border policemen beat the two in an isolated wood, the report said.

"Each one of them carried a club and administered beatings. One of them asked if my chest was all right and hit me in the chest. There were three who hit me," said Moussa, breathing heavily through a hospital mask.
"One of them pointed an M-16 rifle at my head -- he pointed the rifle next to my ear and told me: 'Now you'll get out of here. If I see you again, I will kill you. You must die'."
Showing his bloodied right side to the camera, Ghneim said the border policemen had tied his leg to a jeep and dragged him along the ground for 150 to 200 metres (yards).
The television said Ghneim managed to make his way to a main street where Israelis picked him up in their car and took him to hospital for treatment.
